newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech insurer sees loss after bank fails.
newsitem.headline: Czech insurer sees loss after bank fails.

text.p: Losses from the failed Kreditni Banka a.s. forced Czech insurer, Ceska Pojistovna a.s., to cut its net 1996 earnings forecast Thursday to a loss from its original forecast of a 470 million Czech crowns ($17.73 million) profit.

Company officials said Thursday that Pojistovna should be able to cover the 5.9 billion crowns ($222.6 million) in its liabilities in the bank through its reserves augmented by a 1.14 billion crown ($43 million) rights issue and 1996 revenues.
Still, Pojistovna board member Ladislav Bartonicek told a news conference after an extraordinary general meeting that the insurance company might post a net loss for the year.
"It should not be a dramatically negative number," he said. Pojistovna was stung by last month's collapse of the medium-sized Plzen-based Kreditni Banka in which it holds a 66 percent stake.
Local analysts have blamed Kreditni's failure on dubious loans made by banking management to interests connected to shareholders, and the issue has become political football.
The Czech cabinet on Wednesday assigned three ministers to lead a criminal investigation into the bank's collapse.
